div.div:
Organization = TSG (Tenant Service Group)
The licensing and flex credit boundary. Set once when the
deployment profile is mapped in the Customer Support Portal.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 406px; height: 1px; padding-top: 219px; margin-left: 15px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Workspace = SCM Workspace
The team boundary. Provisioning an integration to a workspace
decides which teams may use it, and sets that team's budget
and rate ceiling. Admin access is governed by SBAC roles.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 406px; height: 1px; padding-top: 331px; margin-left: 15px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Integration one provider connection
Holds the provider credential, the model allowlist, and the
pricing adjust multiplier that turns list price into your
effective rate. Identified in every call by its slug.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 406px; height: 1px; padding-top: 443px; margin-left: 15px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Gateway API key one per application ← the pivot
Carries scoped permissions, its own budget and rate limit, an
expiry, and JSON metadata tags you define:
{ app: chatbot, env: prod, team: platform, cc: 4820 }

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 406px; height: 1px; padding-top: 555px; margin-left: 15px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Arrives bearing that key. The gateway stamps the log record
with the key, its metadata, the integration, the model, the token
counts, and the computed cost.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 78px; margin-left: 463px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 113px; margin-left: 479px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Prompt log native storage, 1 year retention
• Trace ID
• Full request and response context windows
• Token counts, request and response
• Total cost for the call
• Model invoked
• Provider integration used
• The API key that made the call
• Request timing and latency
Event log native + Strata Logging Service
• Audit, authentication, traffic, metrics
• Streams to SIEM and SOAR over OpenTelemetry
Prompt log export to your own bucket is Hybrid only.
If compliance needs prompts in storage you control,
that requirement picks the deployment model.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 78px; margin-left: 943px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 113px; margin-left: 959px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Not from your identity provider.
SSO and Cloud Identity Engine govern who can log
into Strata Cloud Manager. They do not tag traffic.
There is no directory group carried on the request.
Groups are metadata you define.
1. You attach JSON tags to each gateway API key.
2. Requests inherit those tags into the logs.
3. In Policies & Profiles, a budget or rate policy
matches on a Condition Key with includes and
excludes value lists.
4. Group by Key then applies the cap per value
of that key rather than to the matched set as
a whole. Group by team and every team gets
its own ceiling from one policy.
So your metadata schema is your chargeback
model. Design it before you issue the first key.

div.b: 1. What you pay Palo Alto Networks

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 489px; margin-left: 479px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.div:
Flex credits, metered by token consumption.
• 1 token = 4 characters
• LLM prompts, MCP calls, and agent-to-agent
traffic all count against the same pool
• Identical pricing for SaaS and Hybrid
• No extra charge for more gateways
Seen in: Customer Support Portal → Products →
Software NGFW Credits → the AI-GW profile row.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 469px; margin-left: 957px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: 2. What you pay the model provider

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 489px; margin-left: 959px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Unchanged by the gateway. AWS, Anthropic, or
Microsoft still bills your provider account directly.
What the gateway adds is a calculated view of that
spend, per call, so you can attribute and cap it:
• Pricing adjust multiplier per integration
0.80 = a 20% negotiated discount
1.20 = a 20% internal showback markup
• Budget limits in USD or tokens, which block
traffic once hit
Seen in: AI Gateway → Observability.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1364px; height: 1px; padding-top: 739px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: The design decision this diagram exists to force

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 763px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Agree the metadata schema before issuing keys.
Every dimension Finance will later want to slice by has to
exist as a tag on the key from day one. A reasonable
starting set:
{ app: ···, team: ···, env: prod|nonprod,
cost_center: ···, owner: ··· }
Retrofitting is painful: budget limits never apply
retroactively, and keys already in production carry the
old tags until they are reissued.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 763px; margin-left: 473px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
One key per application, not one key per tenant.
A shared key collapses every team into a single row in the
logs and makes revocation an outage. The granularity of
your keys is the granularity of your reporting, your rate
limiting, and your blast radius.
Per-user attribution is not automatic.
A shared application key attributes to the application.
If the customer needs cost or audit per end user, that
has to be designed in deliberately — confirm with the
tenant how per-request metadata is accepted before
promising it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 763px; margin-left: 945px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Limits stack, and the most restrictive wins.
• Key level — this application
• Workspace level — this team's use of an integration
• Policy level — organization-wide, scoped by metadata
conditions and group keys
Budget and rate limits cannot be edited once set, by
any organization member. Get the numbers right the
first time, or plan to recreate the object.
